ujjain.s: Ujjain is an ancient city in central India on the Shipra River, one of the seven sacred cities of Hinduism. It was a major commercial and administrative centre on routes linking northern India with the western coast.

ukiyo-e.s: Ukiyo-e, meaning 'pictures of the floating world', is a genre of Japanese woodblock prints and paintings that flourished from the seventeenth to the nineteenth centuries. It depicted actors, courtesans, landscapes and scenes of urban life.

ukraine.s: Ukraine is a country in eastern Europe whose fertile steppe lands have been contested by many powers. Much of it formed part of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, where the Khmelnytsky uprising of 1648 began the loss of eastern territories to Russia.

ulama.s: The ulama are the community of Muslim religious scholars, trained in Islamic law, theology and scripture. They staffed courts, schools and mosques and often mediated between rulers and subjects.

ulpian.s: Ulpian was a Roman jurist of the early third century CE and one of the most influential legal writers in Roman history. He served as praetorian prefect under Severus Alexander and was killed by the Praetorian Guard.

ulugh-beg.s: Ulugh Beg was a Timurid ruler and astronomer, a grandson of Timur, who governed Samarkand for decades and died in 1449. He built a great observatory and madrasa in Samarkand and sponsored astronomical tables of remarkable accuracy.

ulugh-beg-observatory.s: The Ulugh Beg Observatory was an astronomical observatory built in Samarkand in the 1420s by the Timurid ruler Ulugh Beg. Its huge meridian arc allowed precise measurements, and the astronomers who worked there produced a star catalogue and astronomical tables.

umar-din.s: Umar Din was a sultan of the Walashma dynasty in the Adal Sultanate in the sixteenth century. The Adal Sultanate profile notes that Imam Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi held real power as leader of the jihad against Christian Ethiopia while maintaining a nominal Walashma sultan,…

umar-ibn-al-khattab.s: Umar ibn al-Khattab was the second caliph of the Rashidun Caliphate, ruling from 634 to 644 CE. Under his leadership Muslim armies conquered Syria, Iraq, Egypt and much of Iran, and he established key institutions such as the diwan for paying soldiers and garrison cities.

umayyad-caliphate.s: The Umayyad Caliphate was the second Islamic caliphate, ruled by the Umayyad family from Damascus from 661 to 750 CE. It expanded Muslim rule from Iberia and North Africa to Central Asia and the Indus valley, and established Arabic as the language of administration.

umayyad-conquest-of-hispania.s: The Umayyad conquest of Hispania was the Muslim conquest of most of the Iberian Peninsula beginning in 711 CE. Forces led by Tariq ibn Ziyad crossed from North Africa and defeated the Visigothic king Roderic, and within a few years most of the peninsula was under Umayyad control.

umayyad-conquest-of-sind.s: The Umayyad conquest of Sind was the campaign of 711 CE in which forces led by Muhammad ibn Qasim conquered Sind, in the lower Indus valley in present-day Pakistan. It brought the region under the Umayyad Caliphate and marked the eastern limit of early Arab expansion into…

unequal-treaties.s: Unequal treaties is a term for agreements imposed on East Asian states by Western powers in the nineteenth century, granting privileges such as extraterritoriality, fixed tariffs and treaty ports. China and Japan were both subject to them.

unesco-world-heritage-site.s: A UNESCO World Heritage Site is a place recognised by the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization as having outstanding cultural or natural value. The Elamite Confederation profile notes that the Chogha Zanbil ziggurat built under Untash-Napirisha…

union-of-krewo.s: The Union of Krewo was an agreement of 1385 under which Grand Duke Jogaila of Lithuania agreed to accept Catholic Christianity and marry Queen Jadwiga of Poland, becoming King of Poland. It created a personal union between Poland and Lithuania.

union-of-lublin.s: The Union of Lublin was the agreement of 1569 that transformed the personal union of Poland and Lithuania into a single state, the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth. The two parts retained separate administrations and armies but shared an elected monarch and a common Sejm.

united-nations.s: The United Nations is an international organisation founded in 1945 to maintain peace and promote cooperation among states, with its headquarters in New York. The Hittite Empire profile notes that a reproduction of the Egyptian–Hittite peace treaty of Kadesh hangs at the…

united-states.s: The United States is a federal republic in North America that became independent from Britain in 1776 and grew into a major world power. It defeated the Spanish Empire in 1898, acquiring Spain's remaining overseas colonies, and was the principal adversary of the Empire of…

universal-suffrage.s: Universal suffrage is the right of all adult citizens to vote, regardless of property, class or, in its full form, sex. The German Empire introduced universal male suffrage for elections to the Reichstag in 1871.

untash-napirisha.s: Untash-Napirisha was a king of Elam in the fourteenth century BCE. He built the religious complex of Chogha Zanbil near Susa, centred on a great ziggurat.

uparika.s: An uparika was a provincial governor in the Gupta Empire. The Gupta Empire profile explains that the empire was divided into provinces called bhuktis, each administered by an uparika, frequently a member of the royal family.

upemba-depression.s: The Upemba Depression is a low-lying basin of lakes, marshes and fertile land along the upper Lualaba River in the south-east of the present-day Democratic Republic of the Congo. Archaeological sites there show long continuous occupation.

upper-egypt.s: Upper Egypt is the southern part of Egypt, the narrow Nile Valley stretching from around Memphis southwards to the First Cataract at Aswan. It was home to Thebes, the religious centre of the New Kingdom.

upper-mesopotamia.s: Upper Mesopotamia is the northern part of the land between the Tigris and Euphrates, covering parts of present-day northern Iraq, north-eastern Syria and south-eastern Turkey. Rain-fed agriculture and trade routes supported cities such as Assur and Nineveh, making it the…

ur.s: Ur was an ancient Sumerian city in southern Mesopotamia, near the former course of the Euphrates in present-day Iraq. It reached its height as the capital of the Third Dynasty of Ur, or Neo-Sumerian Empire, under Ur-Nammu and his successors, who built its great ziggurat.

ural-mountains.s: The Ural Mountains are a north–south mountain range in Russia, traditionally regarded as the boundary between Europe and Asia. The Russian Empire profile notes that under Ivan IV Russian expansion crossed the Urals into Siberia, a process accelerated by Yermak Timofeyevich's…

urdu.s: Urdu is an Indo-Aryan language closely related to Hindi, written in a Perso-Arabic script and rich in Persian and Arabic vocabulary. It developed in northern India from the interaction of local speech with the Persian of the ruling elites.

urf.s: Urf is a term for customary law, and in the Safavid Empire it referred to the royal law administered through the Shah's courts. The Safavid Empire profile explains that while Shia judges applied religious law to personal status and family matters, urf handled criminal,…

ur-nammu.s: Ur-Nammu was the founder of the Third Dynasty of Ur, or Neo-Sumerian Empire, who established his rule around 2112 BCE after the collapse of the Akkadian Empire. He is credited with the Code of Ur-Nammu, one of the oldest known law codes, and with major building projects…

urshu.s: Urshu was an ancient city in northern Syria or south-eastern Anatolia, besieged by the Hittites during their early expansion. A Hittite text describing the siege provides rare detail on early siege warfare.

uruguay.s: Uruguay is a country in South America on the east bank of the Río de la Plata. In the early nineteenth century the territory, then known as the Cisplatine Province, was contested between Brazil and Argentina, and the costly war over it ended with Uruguayan independence in 1828.

uruk.s: Uruk was one of the oldest and largest cities of ancient Sumer, in southern Mesopotamia, and is associated with the early development of writing and urban life. It was the city of the legendary king Gilgamesh.

ur-zababa.s: Ur-Zababa was a king of the Sumerian city of Kish in the late third millennium BCE. According to tradition, the future Sargon of Akkad served as his cupbearer.

us-oil-embargo-against-japan.s: The US oil embargo against Japan was the cutting off of American oil exports to Japan in 1941, imposed in response to Japanese expansion in Indochina. The Empire of Japan profile notes that Japan imported approximately eighty percent of its oil from the United States.

usman-dan-fodio.s: Usman dan Fodio was a Fulani Islamic scholar and reformer who led a jihad against the Hausa kingdoms beginning in 1804 and founded the Sokoto Caliphate. His movement created one of the largest states in nineteenth-century Africa and inspired other reform movements across West…

uss-missouri.s: The USS Missouri was a United States Navy battleship of the Iowa class, commissioned during the Second World War. On 2 September 1945 the formal Japanese surrender was signed aboard it in Tokyo Bay.

uthman-ibn-affan.s: Uthman ibn Affan was the third caliph of the Rashidun Caliphate, ruling from 644 to 656 CE. His reign saw continued expansion and the compilation of a standard text of the Quran, but accusations of favouring his Umayyad kinsmen provoked growing discontent.

uyghurs.s: The Uyghurs are a Turkic people who founded a powerful khaganate on the Mongolian steppe in the mid-eighth century after overthrowing the Second Turkic Khaganate in alliance with others. The Uyghur Khaganate became a major ally of the Tang Dynasty before its collapse in 840.

uzama.s: The uzama were the hereditary noble chiefs of the Benin kingdom, who held significant power under the earlier Ogiso system. The Benin Empire profile describes how the Oba dynasty centralised royal authority against them, and how Oba Ewuare the Great removed the uzama chiefs'…

uzbekistan.s: Uzbekistan is a country in Central Asia covering much of historic Transoxiana, including the cities of Samarkand, Bukhara and Tashkent. It was the heartland of the Timurid Empire, whose capital was Samarkand, and an important part of the Chagatai Empire.

uzbeks.s: The Uzbeks are a Turkic people of Central Asia whose name derives from the nomadic confederation that formed in the fifteenth century. Under Muhammad Shaybani they conquered Transoxiana from the Timurids around 1500, ending Timurid rule there and driving Babur south.

uzun-hasan.s: Uzun Hasan was the ruler of the Aq Qoyunlu Turkmen confederation, who died in 1478. He built a powerful state in eastern Anatolia, Iraq and western Iran but was defeated by the Ottomans at Otlukbeli in 1473.
